source.title: From GPT-4 to Expert-Endorsed Athlete Guidance: A Delphi Consensus on Sleep and Jet Lag

paper.citation: Vitale J, McCall A, Athlete Travel & Sleep Interest Group (ATSIG), et al. From GPT-4 to Expert-Endorsed Athlete Guidance: A Delphi Consensus on Sleep and Jet Lag. Sports Medicine. 2026. doi:10.1007/s40279-026-02484-7.
paper.abstract: This modified Delphi study asked an international panel of 17 sleep, travel, sport-science, clinical, and elite-athlete-support experts to review and revise 20 GPT-4-derived guidance items on athlete sleep and jet lag. The process converted preliminary model output into expert-endorsed material while retaining two topics that did not reach consensus.
paper.tldr: Expert review produced consensus on 18 of 20 athlete sleep and jet-lag guidance items, while injury-risk wording and sleep-aid or melatonin guidance remained unresolved. The study supports AI as a drafting aid under expert governance, not as an independent authority.
paper.methods: Seventeen purposively selected experts completed two modified Delphi rounds. Experts rated the appropriateness of draft answers, provided revisions, and re-rated steering-committee-adapted items. Consensus was evaluated with rating distributions, interquartile ranges, and round-to-round comparisons.
paper.findings: Consensus increased from 15 of 20 items in round one to 18 of 20 in round two. Injury-risk guidance remained near-threshold non-consensus, and sleep-aid or melatonin guidance remained non-consensus in both rounds. Expert revision repeatedly identified insufficient athlete specificity, misalignment with evidence, formatting problems, and imprecise or misleading draft content.
paper.limitations: The panel was small, purposively selected, and drawn from experts already involved in the earlier language-model evaluation. Delphi consensus represents agreement within that panel, not clinical effectiveness or universal guidance. The study did not test whether the recommendations improved sleep, travel adaptation, health, or performance outcomes.
paper.practicalImplications: Use the expert-endorsed content as a structured starting point for individualized sleep and travel planning. Treat injury-risk claims, melatonin, and other sleep-aid decisions as unresolved or clinically governed topics, and preserve human review for any AI-generated athlete guidance.
paper.athleteDev: Teach athletes repeatable sleep, light-exposure, caffeine, and travel-planning behaviors while adapting timing to destination, schedule, individual response, and medical context. Avoid presenting a generic AI answer as a personalized prescription.
paper.rtp: The study did not evaluate rehabilitation or return to sport. Sleep and travel management may support readiness during recovery, but the consensus items provide no clearance criterion, reinjury estimate, or condition-specific return-to-play protocol.
